What are the exact starting materials an.answer: Starting materials: (1) TiO2 from Cosmo Chemical Co., 0.35 µm particle size, 98.0% purity; (2) TiH2 from Sejong Materials, <635 mesh, 99.3% purity; (3) Fe from BASF, 5 µm particle size, 99.7% purity; (4) Mn from Alfa Aesar, <325 mesh, 99.3% purity; (5) Carbon black from Korea carbon black Co., 20 nm particle size, 99.0% purity.

What are the specific PECS/SPS processin.answer: PECS conditions: (1) Temperature range 1373-1573K; (2) Mechanical pressure 20 MPa; (3) Holding time 3-10 minutes; (4) Heating rates 27 K/min (TiO2 route) or 50 K/min (TiH2 route); (5) Electric current 1100-1200 A; (6) Voltage 3.0-3.5 V; (7) Graphite die (22.85 mm diameter); (8) Vacuum 5-11 Pa.

How does TiH2 compare to TiO2 as startin.answer: TiH2 advantages: (1) No carbon addition required, avoiding carbon contamination; (2) Direct decomposition TiH2 → Ti + H2; (3) Produces more FeTi and Fe2Ti phases; (4) Lower processing temperature (1373-1473K vs 1503-1573K); (5) Cleaner reaction pathway without carbide formation.

What hydrogen storage performance was ac.answer: Hydrogen storage performance: (1) First cycle (activation): 0.11 wt% H at 673K; (2) Third cycle (optimal): 1.17 wt% H for 50-300 min at 303K, 29 bar; (3) Eighth cycle (degraded): 0.93 wt% H at 39 min; (4) Test conditions: 303K, 29 bar initial H2 pressure; (5) Activation required at 673K for first cycle.

What phases were identified by XRD analy.answer: XRD identified phases: (1) From TiO2 route: FeTi, Fe2Ti, TiC, FeTiO3, residual Ti and Fe; (2) From TiH2 route: FeTi, Fe2Ti, Ti, Mn, FeMn3, residual Fe; (3) TiH2 route produces more FeTi and Fe2Ti phases; (4) TiO2 route forms carbides (TiC) due to carbon reduction; (5) Background suggests slight amorphous content.

What ball milling conditions were used?.answer: Ball milling conditions: (1) Speed: 120 rpm; (2) Duration: 24 hours; (3) Container: hermetically sealed, Ar-filled stainless steel (307 cm³ volume); (4) Balls: stainless steel, 6 mm diameter, 1260 g total weight; (5) Medium: hexane 100 cc; (6) Sample weight: 50 g; (7) Equipment: low energy horizontal ball mill; (8) Result: fine agglomerates with average size 256 nm (range 70-650 nm).

What characterization techniques were em.answer: Characterization techniques: (1) XRD: Rigaku D/max 2200, Cu Kα radiation, 40 kV, scan speed 5°/min, 2θ range 20°-80°; (2) FE-SEM: Philips X130 SFEG for microstructure; (3) DLS: ELS-8000 Photal Otsuka for particle size in ethanol; (4) Carbon-sulfur analysis: Eltra CS-8000 with steel standard calibration; (5) SPS equipment: Sumitomo 2040 with graphite die.
